A one-column tree (locations, folders, product structure), drawn by AtomicAUI TreeView: rows with no border and no fill (paint text), a plain text-paint arrow to fold a parent, each level further in by the TreeView indent. Only the picked row is filled.
recipes.behaviour: Keep role="tree" and role="treeitem" with aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset and one item with tabindex="0" (the picked one, else the first; the others -1). Keep the old tree's item identifiers (its data-key or id values) as they were; a restyle adds no data-key the old tree lacked. A parent item carries aria-expanded: a click on its arrow (aui-tree-view-chevron) opens or closes it, Right opens it, Left closes it (show or hide its role="group" of child items, and set aria-expanded and data-expanded); the arrow never picks. A tree that never folds (the React Tree with foldable={false}) is the same markup with every group open and each aui-tree-view-chevron empty, and no fold script. A click on a row (data-aui-tree-view-row), Enter or Space picks its item, a parent too; here North plant is picked. The picked item takes data-selected and aria-selected="true", and its row aui-color-solid-surface-alt in place of aui-color-text-surface; every other item keeps aria-selected="false" and its row aui-color-text-surface. Up, Down, Home and End move the focus between visible items. All of it is your own script: the class list has no state. Rows and arrows sit on the surface: never draw a row as a button, never a border or a tonal box (check-standard fails it). The indent is TreeView's: do not add padding.

recipes.when: Rows and columns of data, display only.
recipes.behaviour: nothing, unless a column must be narrow or the table picks rows. Columns share the width equally; a narrow column takes the layout class aui-width-<n> (for example aui-width-96) on its header cell and on every cell of that column, never a width attribute on col, td or th and no width in your CSS. A selection column is the first column with an empty header cell and the checkbox recipe (recipes/field.md) in each cell, all with aui-width-64, as the React control column is 64 px wide; what a tick does is yours (OPEN: if unknown). One row to pick: the table-row-selected recipe (a click on the row) or table-row-radio (a radio in that column). A table whose columns do not fit 390 px is table-scroll (recipes/table-wide.md), never a wrapper box. A status or State column puts the chip-status recipe (recipes/chip.md) in every cell. When you restyle an existing table, a status that was plain text stays plain text: the chip only where the source already showed a status badge. A picture placeholder in a cell uses table-picture-tile (recipes/picture-tile.md).

recipes.when: Views of the same thing; the first tab is active.
recipes.behaviour: Copy the block whole, panels included, and load aui/aui-behaviour.js in the page head: it moves focus with the arrow keys and switches on Enter, Space and click; without it nothing switches. The block is two tabs with their two panels, written the way the page needs them: every tab has aria-controls naming its panel, every panel has role="tabpanel" and aria-labelledby naming its tab, and every panel but the picked one takes the layout class aui-display-none (the hidden attribute does not hide a panel). A tab without its panel selects and shows nothing: for another tab copy one tab and one panel together with new ids (tab, panel and the two references). Change the text only; the panel holds the page content of that tab. The steps it must pass: kit/standard/behaviour/tabs.md.

recipes.behaviour: Copy the block whole and load aui/aui-behaviour.js. The Tabs root sets shape none for its tabs; the inset tab row and list explicitly keep soft corners. The list is as wide as its tabs (aui-display-inline-flex), so tabs that keep a width scroll inside the row.

recipes.when: A tab row that runs from edge to edge of the window, under an edge-to-edge top bar: the row has no corners; its tabs keep their gap and their soft corners.
recipes.behaviour: Copy the block whole and load aui/aui-behaviour.js. Put it where it spans the window, with no padded box around it: the tab row (data-aui-tab-row) carries aui-shape-none there, and its tabs start at the window edge, which the page-padding check allows for this row only. With space around the row copy pane-tabs-header or tabs-gapless from tabs.md, whose row is soft. The tab list carries aui-display-inline-flex: it is as wide as its tabs, so a tab that keeps a width (aui-width-160) or a minimum width (aui-min-width-160) is never squeezed. Tabs that do not fit scroll sideways inside the row, and the page does not. The panel has no padding, so what it holds starts at the window edge with the tabs: use this row over what spans the window (a table). A page of panes takes its tabs in a pane header: pane-tabs-header in tabs.md.

recipes.when: A pane whose 28 px header band holds tabs instead of a title: each tab panel is the padded row of the pane and holds the body card.
recipes.behaviour: Keep the Tabs root around the page frame so the tab list in the header and the panels under it share one part. Keep data-aui-panes, data-aui-pane, data-aui-pane-header, data-aui-tab-row and data-aui-pane-body. Load aui/aui-behaviour.js, pair every tab with its panel by id, and hide each inactive panel with aui-display-none. The header pads the tab row 8 px at the sides (PN3) and the tabs fill its 28 px, so nothing is between the band and the tab row. The tab list sits in the tab row (data-aui-tab-row, a scroll area with only its viewport) and carries aui-display-inline-flex: it is as wide as its tabs, so a tab that keeps a width (aui-width-160) or a minimum width (aui-min-width-160) is never squeezed. Tabs that do not fit scroll sideways inside the row, with no bar, and the page never scrolls sideways. Keep the row and the list class for two tabs too, and never give the row a width or an overflow class. Each tab panel comes directly under the header as the row of the pane: it is padded 4 / 8, so the body card in it starts at the left edge of the tab row, 4 px under the header (PN6). The scroll area between the panel and the card has no padding and scrolls what is taller than the pane. Put the form, sections or text of a tab inside its card, which pads it 4 / 8 as in every pane. For a table, a tree or a drawing frame, copy pane-tabs-header-fill (recipes/tabs-fill.md) instead: its filling card is the only child of the panel. Never put a filling card inside this scroll area: it grows past the pane. This is the only padded tab panel: under a tab list that is not in a pane header the panel has no padding (the tabs recipe). Never put another padded box inside the panel, and never put a panel inside the card.

recipes.when: A pane whose header band holds tabs, for a tab that shows a table, a tree or a drawing frame: the card fills the panel; a table or a drawing frame scrolls inside its own frame, a tree inside the scroll area of tree-scroll.
recipes.behaviour: Everything pane-tabs-header (recipes/tabs.md) says about the Tabs root, the markers, the tab row and the padded panel. The card (data-aui-pane-body="fill") is the only child of each panel: no scroll area around it, and never a second box beside it. Below 768 px aui/aui-behaviour.js makes it as high as what it holds, 192 px at least. Replace the table with your table or drawing frame, or with the whole tree-scroll block (recipes/tree.md) for a tree. A table keeps what makes this one scroll inside the card with its header in place, as table-scroll does (recipes/table-wide.md): data-aui-min-inline-size, the style attribute with --aui-table-min-inline-size (128 px for each column, 48 px for a column of one icon button) and the aui-table-scroll-clip div around its header; without them the rows below the pane cannot be reached. The last column holds one icon button: aui-width-48 on its header cell, which has an aria-label and no text, and on every cell of the column; the cells are centred (aui-text-align-center).

recipes.behaviour: Keep the bar whole: the two icon buttons keep their aria-label, the range text is "<first>-<last> of <total>", and the page-size control is the closed select (field-select look: a trigger with the value and a chevron, aria-label "Results per page"). Never replace it with a native select, an input or plain text. Previous is disabled on the first page and Next on the last. Without React the bar draws nothing by itself: your own script sets the range text and the disabled marks, and the select shows the closed look only (aui-behaviour.js opens a select that has aria-controls and a list: the select-open recipe in field.md, when the page size must be chosen from a list).

recipes.when: A top bar that runs from edge to edge of the window: only the bar loses its corners; its buttons stay soft.
recipes.behaviour: The bar is 36 px high (PN11). Copy its whole class list. At the window edges its four radius classes are none; never replace its shape class with aui-shape-none, which would also square its buttons.

recipes.when: A top bar with space around it: the bar and its buttons keep their soft corners.
recipes.behaviour: Copy the whole class list when the bar has space around it. Keep the default soft radius and do not add radius-none classes.

recipes.when: Two or more page links in a top bar. Each link keeps its address and role; the current page is marked without changing its look.
recipes.behaviour: Keep each link as an <a href role="link"> with the whole link class list. Give exactly the current page aria-current="page". The edge-to-edge bar has square corners only on itself; its buttons stay soft. A bar with space around it keeps these links and takes the bar class list of top-bar-inset. This block has no narrow form: the React NavLinks folds the links into a "Menu" below 768 px (kit/recipes/app-frame.md) and this block does not, so a bar with many links can run wider than a 390 px window (GAPS.md).
